desc: Largest language family by speakers. Includes Germanic, Romance, Slavic, Indo-Aryan, Iranian branches. Languages: English, Spanish, Hindi, Bengali, Portuguese, Russian, German, French. Originated from Pontic-Caspian steppe (Yamnaya culture).
fact: 3.5B speakers · English, Hindi, Spanish · Germanic, Romance, Slavic, Indo-Aryan · Yamnaya origin

desc: Second largest language family. Includes Chinese (Mandarin, Cantonese), Tibetan, Burmese. Over 400 languages. Chinese is the most spoken language in the world by native speakers.
fact: 1.4B speakers · Chinese, Tibetan, Burmese · 400+ languages · Yellow River origin

desc: Largest African language family. Includes Bantu languages (Swahili, Zulu, Xhosa), Yoruba, Igbo, Fula. Over 1,500 languages. Swahili has 100M+ speakers as a lingua franca.
fact: 600M speakers · Bantu (Swahili, Zulu) · 1,500+ languages · West African origin

desc: Includes Arabic, Hebrew, Amharic, Somali, Hausa. Ancient Egyptian was Afroasiatic. Over 350 languages. Arabic has 310M+ native speakers. Originated in the Levant or Northeast Africa.
fact: 500M speakers · Arabic, Hebrew, Amharic · 350+ languages · Ancient Egyptian

desc: Languages of Maritime Southeast Asia, Oceania, Madagascar. Includes Malay/Indonesian, Javanese, Tagalog, Vietnamese, Hawaiian. Over 1,200 languages. Originated in Taiwan (Formosan branch).
fact: 400M speakers · Malay, Javanese, Tagalog · 1,200+ languages · Taiwan origin

desc: Major language family of South India. Includes Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam. Also Brahui in Pakistan. 70+ languages. Tamil is one of the longest-surviving classical languages.
fact: 250M speakers · Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam · South India · Ancient Tamil

desc: Includes Turkish, Uzbek, Azerbaijani, Kazakh, Uyghur. Spread by Turkic migrations from Central Asia. Over 40 languages. Turkish is the most spoken. Originated in Mongolia/southern Siberia.
fact: 200M speakers · Turkish, Uzbek, Kazakh · Central Asian origin · Turkic migrations

desc: Controversial language family. Japanese (125M speakers) and Korean (80M) are often classified separately but share structural similarities. Ryukyuan languages are also included.
fact: 130M speakers · Japanese, Korean · Ryukyuan · Possible Altaic connection
